newsitem.title: MEXICO: Founder of Mexican debtor group arrested.
newsitem.headline: Founder of Mexican debtor group arrested.

text.p: The founder of a grass-roots debtors' activist group was arrested on Wednesday on various charges including robbery and conspiracy, officials in this western Mexican city said.

Maximiano Barboza Llamas, founder of the popular El Barzon debtors' movement, posted bail but decided to remain in jail in support of fellow group members that were also arrested and did not make bail, state police said.
Dozens of protesters surrounded the city hall building following Barboza's arrest and demanded that the charges against him be dropped.

Police said charges were brought against Barboza, who no longer leads the group he founded, and others by a bank lawyer who claims he was harassed and robbed by the group and also dipped in honey and covered in chicken feathers.

Barboza set up El Barzon, which means "the yoke" in Spanish, in 1993 as a rural protest group to demand relief for farmers' unpaid loans. The group's popularity boomed following the 1994 peso crisis and now claims more than a half million members, mostly from the middle class.

Barboza lost leadership of the group shortly after the peso crisis following a power struggle with current leader Jose Quirino Salas, but is still considered an important figure within the group and a leader in western Jalisco state.
Barzon protests have become an almost daily sight in Mexico and the group has been instrumental in pressuring the government to provide debt-relief programmes, political analysts say.

Another group of about 100 El Barzon supporters clashed with police in Mexico City on Wednesday, causing injuries among a few protesters and police, Mexico City police said. Four of the protesters were arrested, police said.
